bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price volatility — Exposure to fluctuations in cotton, polyester and other fibre prices, influenced by international trade dynamics, weather conditions and government policies; sudden price spikes can affect cost structures and margins.
- Global economic uncertainty — A significant portion of India's textile output is export-oriented; slowdown in key markets such as the US and Europe, coupled with inflationary pressures and geopolitical tensions, may adversely affect demand.
- Foreign exchange risk — Exposure to currency fluctuations given considerable export revenues; sharp movements in foreign exchange rates could impact profitability.
- Competition — Intense competition from countries such as Bangladesh, Vietnam and Turkey, which enjoy cost advantages in labor and logistics, pressuring pricing and profitability in international markets.
- Regulatory and compliance challenges — Increasingly stringent global requirements on sustainability, environmental protection and labor standards necessitate continuous investment in compliance; failure to adapt may lead to loss of market access and reputational risk.
- Operational risks — Rising energy costs, logistics challenges and dependence on migrant labor pose operational risks, especially for small and medium enterprises within the textile ecosystem.
- Technological obsolescence — Rapid technological changes in manufacturing, automation and digital integration require continuous upgradation; companies that lag behind may lose competitiveness.

- R&D-driven flexibility to produce a range of yarn products — micro fibre, regular POY of fine to coarse denier, Full Dull, Semi Dull, Bright Yarns, Doped Dyed Yarn, recycled yarns, Fire Retardant and Anti Microbial yarns.

outlook.body: The Company has already installed a direct melt transfer line to the POY plant, bypassing the chip-making process to save energy from cooling, cutting, packing, transporting and re-heating/extruding, while also assuring uninterrupted polymer supply to the POY lines for better production efficiency. The Company is in the process of installing new POY production lines with better quality, higher efficiency and lower energy consumption and material wastage.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Domestic demand supported by rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, changing consumer preferences, growing penetration of organised/branded apparel and expansion of e-commerce and digital retail.
- Government policy support via the PLI Scheme for Textiles, PM MITRA Mega Textile Parks and initiatives on technical textiles, technology upgradation and sustainability, expected to strengthen competitiveness and attract investment.
- Global buyers diversifying sourcing away from China expected to help India capture a larger share of international markets, particularly the US and Europe, aided by pending FTAs with the UK and EU.
- Moderate pace of capacity additions in certain segments of the polyester yarn industry expected to support a more balanced demand-supply environment over the medium term.
- Challenges from raw material price volatility, rising energy costs, global economic uncertainty and compliance with evolving environmental/labor standards may continue to pressure margins.
